hook.situation: Your Korean friend tells you about a stressful day: someone at work was 'pretending not to know,' they 'almost cried' during a movie, and they're 'guessing the boss is angry.' You understand the gist but can't quite follow the grammar gluing it together. Those three reactions — faking something, narrowly avoiding something, and inferring from clues — each need their own structure in Korean.
objectives: Use -는 척하다 to say someone is pretending or faking a state or action
Use -(으)ㄹ 뻔했어요 to describe a close call — something that almost happened but didn't
Use -나 보다 / -(으)ㄴ가 보다 to make an evidence-based guess about someone else's situation
hook.whyItMatters: These three patterns appear constantly in Korean storytelling and conversation. Without them, you can describe facts but not the texture of human experience — the white lies, the near-misses, and the inferences you draw about the people around you. Master all three and your Korean instantly sounds more natural and more adult.

grammarNotes.title: -는 척하다 — pretend / act like
grammarNotes.func: Use -는 척하다 to say someone pretends to do or be something — putting on an act that doesn't match reality. It marks behavior that's deliberately faked.

formTable.when: Action verb, present (pretend to be doing now)
formTable.ex: 자다 → 자는 척하다 (pretend to be sleeping)

formTable.when: Action verb, past (pretend to have done)
formTable.ex: 먹다 → 먹은 척하다 / 보다 → 본 척하다
괜찮다 → 괜찮은 척하다 / 아프다 → 아픈 척하다
학생이다 → 학생인 척하다 (pretend to be a student)

examples.en: My friend came over, but I pretended to be asleep.
examples.note: 자다 is happening now → present -는 척하다.

examples.ko: 그 영화 안 봤는데 본 척했어요.
examples.romanization: geu yeonghwa an bwanneunde bon cheokaesseoyo.
examples.en: I hadn't seen that movie, but I pretended I had.
examples.note: 보다 done before now → past -(으)ㄴ 척하다 (본).

examples.en: I was actually sick, but I pretended I was fine.
Don't act like you know when you don't.
examples.note: 알다 is a ㄹ-verb, present sense → 아는 척 (ㄹ drops before -는).

keyPoint.label: -는 척하다 vs -(으)ㄴ 척하다
keyPoint.body: The ending works just like a modifier (관형사형): an action happening now takes -는 (자는 척), a finished action takes -(으)ㄴ (먹은 척), and adjectives also take -(으)ㄴ (아픈 척). You can swap 척 for 체 with no change in meaning (자는 체하다), though 척 is more common in everyday speech.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 척했어요 sounds like [처캐써요] — ㄱ + ㅎ merge into the aspirated [ㅋ].

drill.instruction: Turn each cue into '(I) pretended to ~' using -는/-(으)ㄴ 척했어요.
drill.model: 안 자다 / 자다 → 안 자는데 자는 척했어요.
items: 잘 모르다 / 알다 → 잘 모르는데 잘 ___ 척했어요.
안 먹다 / 먹다 → 밥을 안 먹었는데 ___ 척했어요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English 'pretend to be fine' makes learners reach for -는, but 괜찮다 is an adjective, so it takes the adjective modifier -(으)ㄴ → 괜찮은 척. Only action verbs happening now take -는 척.

grammarNotes.title: -(으)ㄹ 뻔하다 — almost happened (a close call)
grammarNotes.func: Use -(으)ㄹ 뻔하다 to say something nearly happened but didn't — a near miss. It's almost always used in the past tense (-(으)ㄹ 뻔했어요) because the close call already happened.

formTable.when: Verb stem ends in a vowel
Verb stem ends in a consonant (받침)
formTable.ex: 죽다 → 죽을 뻔하다 / 늦다 → 늦을 뻔하다

examples.en: I almost fell on the street.
examples.note: 넘어지다 ends in a vowel → -ㄹ 뻔하다; past 뻔했어요.

examples.en: I overslept and almost got to school late.
examples.note: 늦다 ends in 받침 ㅈ → -을 뻔하다.

examples.en: I almost cried when I heard that story.
examples.note: 울다 is a ㄹ-stem; ㄹ stays before 뻔 → 울 뻔하다.

examples.en: I spilled water and the book almost got wet.
examples.note: 젖다 ends in 받침 → -을 뻔하다; the book didn't actually get wet.

keyPoint.label: Always past tense, always 'didn't happen'
keyPoint.body: -(으)ㄹ 뻔했다 means the event did NOT happen — it only came close. So 넘어질 뻔했어요 = 'I almost fell (but didn't).' Don't put the main verb in the past too: say 넘어질 뻔했어요, never 넘어졌을 뻔했어요.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 뻔했어요 sounds like [뻔해써요]; the opening ㅃ is a tense (fortis) sound — keep it hard, not a soft [ㅂ].

drill.instruction: Make a 'close call' sentence with -(으)ㄹ 뻔했어요.
items: 물을 쏟다 → 컵을 건드려서 물을 ___ 뻔했어요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English 'almost fell' is past, so learners put the main verb in the past too. But only 뻔하다 carries the past tense; the action verb stays in -(으)ㄹ form, because the fall never actually happened.

grammarNotes.title: -나 보다 / -(으)ㄴ가 보다 — guessing from evidence
grammarNotes.func: Use -나 보다 / -(으)ㄴ가 보다 to make a guess based on something you can see or hear, like English 'I guess...' or 'It seems...'. You're inferring about a situation rather than stating it as a fact.

formTable.ex: 오다 → 오나 보다 / 먹다 → 먹나 보다
가다 → 갔나 보다 / 자다 → 잤나 보다
춥다 → 추운가 보다 / 바쁘다 → 바쁜가 보다
학생이다 → 학생인가 보다 (guess: must be a student)

examples.ko: 사람들이 우산을 써요. 비가 오나 봐요.
examples.romanization: saramdeuri usaneul sseoyo. biga ona bwayo.
examples.en: People are using umbrellas. I guess it's raining.
examples.note: 오다 is an action verb, present → -나 보다.

examples.ko: 친구가 전화를 안 받아요. 자나 봐요.
examples.romanization: chinguga jeonhwareul an badayo. jana bwayo.
examples.en: My friend isn't answering the phone. I guess they're sleeping.
examples.note: 자다 action verb, present → 자나 봐요.

examples.ko: 불이 꺼져 있어요. 다들 집에 갔나 봐요.
examples.romanization: buri kkeojyeo isseoyo. dadeul jibe ganna bwayo.
examples.en: The lights are off. I guess everyone went home.

examples.ko: 다들 두꺼운 옷을 입었어요. 추운가 봐요.
examples.romanization: dadeul dukkeoun oseul ibeosseoyo. chuunga bwayo.
examples.en: Everyone's wearing thick clothes. I guess it's cold.
examples.note: 춥다 is an adjective → -(으)ㄴ가 보다 (추운가, ㅂ-irregular).

keyPoint.label: -나 보다 vs -(으)ㄹ 것 같다
keyPoint.body: -나 보다 means you're inferring from something you observed ('I see this, so I guess that'). -(으)ㄹ 것 같다 is a softer, more general guess or impression that needs no evidence. Use -나 보다 only when you're reasoning from a clue. (The fuller contrast lives in the conjecture chapter.)

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 봐요 sounds like [봐:요], a contraction of 보아요; keep it one syllable [bwa].

drill.instruction: Given the clue, finish the guess with -나 봐요 / -(으)ㄴ가 봐요.
items: 교실에 아무도 없어요. (수업이 끝나다) → 수업이 ___ 봐요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Learners often attach -(으)ㄴ가 to everything, but action verbs (동사) in the present take -나 보다, while only adjectives and 이다 take -(으)ㄴ가 보다. So 오다 → 오나 봐요, but 춥다 → 추운가 봐요.

extendedVocabulary.english: deep emotion; being moved or touched

exampleSentence.ko: 그 영화 너무 감동적이어서 울 뻔했어요.
exampleSentence.en: That movie was so moving I almost cried.
exampleSentence.note: 감동적이다 = to be moving/touching; 울 뻔했어요 shows the emotional near-miss naturally

exampleSentence.ko: 그 사람 표정을 보니까 많이 두려워하나 봐요.
exampleSentence.en: From that person's expression, I guess they're really afraid.
exampleSentence.note: 두려워하다 is an action verb, so it takes -나 봐요. The visible expression is the evidence.

exampleSentence.ko: 팀장님 말투가 그러는 걸 보니까 화나신 건가 봐요.
exampleSentence.en: The way the team leader is talking, I'm guessing they're angry.
exampleSentence.note: -(으)ㄴ가 봐요 = inferring the emotion from observable evidence (their tone)

exampleSentence.ko: 합격했다는 소식을 듣고 만족스러워서 소리를 지를 뻔했어요.
exampleSentence.en: When I heard I passed, I was so satisfied I almost shouted.
exampleSentence.note: 만족스럽다 = to feel satisfied; 소리를 지르다 = to shout; 지를 뻔했어요 = almost-shouted close call

exampleSentence.ko: 그분이 모르는 척한 것 때문에 신뢰를 잃었어요.
exampleSentence.en: Because he pretended not to know, I lost trust in him.
exampleSentence.note: 모르는 척하다 (pretending not to know) combined with 신뢰를 잃다 (lose trust) — common real-life pairing

exampleSentence.ko: 그분 이야기가 나오면 다들 조용해지는 걸 보니까 많이 존경하나 봐요.
exampleSentence.en: Seeing everyone quiet down when that person comes up, I guess they respect them a lot.
exampleSentence.note: 존경하다 is an action verb, so it takes -나 봐요. The group reaction gives the clue.
성실하다 is an adjective → 성실한 것 같다 (soft opinion); contrast with -나 보다 which implies outside evidence

exampleSentence.ko: 그 사람이 사실대로 말하는 걸 보니까 정직한 사람인가 봐요.
exampleSentence.en: Seeing that person tell the truth, I guess they're an honest person.
exampleSentence.note: 정직한 사람인가 봐요 uses noun phrase 사람인가 봐요 after the adjective modifier 정직한.

extendedVocabulary.english: to be careful; prudent; cautious in decisions

exampleSentence.ko: 그 사람 말을 잘 안 하는 걸 보니까 신중한가 봐요.
exampleSentence.en: They don't say much — I'm guessing they're the careful type.
exampleSentence.note: 신중하다 → -(으)ㄴ가 봐요; inferring personality from observable behavior

extendedVocabulary.english: to be coolheaded; level-headed; cold; detached

exampleSentence.en: I pretended to be coolheaded, but it was actually hard.
exampleSentence.note: 냉정한 척하다 uses the target adjective directly: acting detached even when you are shaken inside.

extendedVocabulary.english: tricky; demanding; picky; hard to satisfy

exampleSentence.ko: 심사 기준이 까다로운가 봐요. 다들 탈락했네요.
exampleSentence.en: I guess the judging criteria are strict — everyone got eliminated.
exampleSentence.note: 까다롭다 → -(으)ㄴ가 봐요 (evidence-based inference from the result); ㅂ-irregular: 까다롭 + 은가 → 까다로운가

extendedVocabulary.english: 'I almost...'; by a narrow margin (near-miss adverb)

exampleSentence.note: 하마터면 always pairs with -(으)ㄹ 뻔했어요 to emphasize the narrowness of the near-miss

extendedVocabulary.english: to pick up on; to sense; to figure out (from cues)

exampleSentence.ko: 걔가 눈치챈 것 같아서 아무것도 모르는 척했어요.
exampleSentence.en: I felt like they were picking up on it, so I pretended not to know anything.
exampleSentence.note: 눈치채다 → trigger for using 척하다: when someone might catch on, you put on the ignorance mask

extendedVocabulary.english: to hide; to conceal (feelings or information)

exampleSentence.en: I pretended to be fine in an attempt to hide my feelings.
exampleSentence.note: 감추려고 (in order to hide) + 척하다 — a very natural Korean expression of masking emotions

extendedVocabulary.english: to be obvious; to show; to give away (that you're faking)

exampleSentence.en: I pretended to be asleep but I guess it was obvious.
exampleSentence.note: 티가 났나 봐요 = evidence-based guess (someone's reaction revealed it); 척하다 + 나 봐요 together in one sentence

extendedVocabulary.english: to tremble; to be shaky (with nerves or emotion)

exampleSentence.en: During my presentation, my voice almost started shaking.
exampleSentence.note: 떨리다 ends in vowel → -ㄹ 뻔했어요; common near-miss emotion verb in presentations and auditions

extendedDialogue.setting: Two coworkers, Jiyeon and Minsu, are eating lunch together and talking about a stressful morning

lines.speaker: 지연
lines.ko: 오늘 오전에 발표하다가 목소리가 떨릴 뻔했어요.
lines.romanization: oneul ojeone balpyohadaga moksoriga tteollil ppeonhaesseoyo.
lines.en: This morning during my presentation, my voice almost started shaking.
lines.grammarNote: 떨리다 = vowel-stem verb → -ㄹ 뻔했어요; the near-miss is past and already resolved

lines.speaker: 민수
lines.ko: 어, 저도 봤는데 엄청 자연스러웠어요. 몰랐어요.
lines.romanization: eo, jeodo bwanneunde eomcheong jayeonseureowosseoyo. mollasseoyo.
lines.en: Oh, I was watching and you were super natural. I couldn't tell.
lines.grammarNote: No grammar point here — a natural supportive reply that makes the 척하다 line in the next turn more impactful

lines.speaker: 지연
lines.ko: 고마워요. 사실 많이 떨렸는데 괜찮은 척했어요.
lines.romanization: gomawoyo. sasil mani tteollyeonneunde gwaenchaneun cheokaesseoyo.
lines.en: Thank you. I was actually shaking a lot, but I pretended to be fine.
lines.grammarNote: 괜찮다 is an adjective → -(으)ㄴ 척하다: 괜찮은 척했어요; confirms the mask was successfully worn

lines.speaker: 민수
lines.ko: 그래요? 팀장님도 잘 모르시는 것 같던데요.
lines.romanization: geuraeyo? timjangnimdo jal moreusineun geot gatdeondeyo.
lines.en: Really? It seemed like the team leader didn't notice either.
lines.grammarNote: -것 같던데요 = a gentle evidence-based impression recalled from the past; softer than -나 봐요 here because the speaker is recounting their own observation

lines.speaker: 지연
lines.ko: 팀장님은 지금 다른 문제로 머리가 복잡한가 봐요.
lines.romanization: timjangnimeun jigeum dareun munjero meoriga bokjapanga bwayo.
lines.en: I think the team leader's head is full of other problems right now.
lines.grammarNote: 복잡하다 = adjective → -(으)ㄴ가 봐요: 복잡한가 봐요; evidence-based inference about someone else's mental state

lines.speaker: 민수
lines.ko: 맞아요. 아침에 표정이 안 좋으시더라고요. 스트레스 많이 받으시나 봐요.
lines.romanization: majayo. achime pyojeongi an joeusideoragoyo. seuteureseu mani badeusinabwayo.
lines.en: Right. Their expression this morning didn't look good. I'm guessing they're under a lot of stress.
lines.grammarNote: 받으시나 봐요 = honorific 시 + -나 봐요. The visible evidence (bad expression) triggers the inference.

lines.speaker: 지연
lines.ko: 하마터면 제가 먼저 물어볼 뻔했는데 참았어요.
lines.romanization: hamateomyeon jega meonjeo mureobol ppeonhaenneunde chamasseoyo.
lines.en: I almost asked first, but I held back.
lines.grammarNote: 하마터면 + 물어보다 (vowel stem) → -ㄹ 뻔했는데; -는데 adds a contrastive note (almost did, but then...)

lines.speaker: 민수
lines.ko: 잘하셨어요. 지금은 모르는 척하는 게 나을 것 같아요.
lines.romanization: jalhasyeosseoyo. jigeumeun moreuneun cheokhaneun ge naeul geot gatayo.
lines.en: Good call. Right now, playing dumb is probably better.
lines.grammarNote: 모르다 = action verb → 모르는 척하다; 하는 게 나을 것 같다 = 'it's probably better to...' — 척하다 appears as a noun-modifying clause here

readingText.title: 지연의 하루 일기 (Jiyeon's Day Diary)
readingText.body: 오늘은 정말 힘든 하루였다. 아침에 중요한 발표가 있었는데, 엄청 긴장해서 울 뻔했다. 발표하는 내내 떨렸지만 괜찮은 척하면서 끝까지 버텼다. 팀장님은 좀 무표정하게 앉아 계셨는데, 뭔가 불만이 있으신가 봐서 마음이 불안했다. 나중에 동료한테 물어봤더니 "요즘 윗사람 때문에 스트레스를 많이 받으시나 봐"라고 했다. 그 말 듣고 조금 안심이 됐다. 퇴근하다가 지갑을 잃어버릴 뻔했다. 하마터면 큰일 날 뻔했는데, 다행히 가방 안쪽에 있었다. 내일은 오늘보다 나은 하루이길 바란다.
readingText.bodyTranslation: Today was a really tough day. There was an important presentation in the morning, and I was so nervous I almost cried. I was shaking the whole time but I pretended to be fine and hung in there to the end. The team leader sat there with a blank expression, and I felt uneasy thinking they seemed to have some complaint. I asked a coworker later, and they said, "It looks like the team leader is under a lot of stress because of upper management these days." Hearing that made me feel a bit relieved. On the way out of the office, I almost lost my wallet. That was almost a disaster, but thankfully it was in the inside pocket of my bag. I hope tomorrow is a better day than today.

comprehensionQuestions.question: Why did Jiyeon pretend to be fine during the presentation?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: She was shaking and almost cried (울 뻔했다), but she put on a mask of composure (괜찮은 척하면서) and pushed through to the end.

comprehensionQuestions.question: How does Jiyeon learn about the team leader's stress? What Korean pattern does she use for this inference?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: She hears it from a coworker. She uses 스트레스를 많이 받으시나 봐 — the -나 봐 pattern (action verb 받다 → 받으시나 봐) because the coworker is making an evidence-based inference, not stating a confirmed fact.

comprehensionQuestions.question: Find every instance of 척하다, 뻔하다, and -나/-(으)ㄴ가 보다 in the text. For each one, explain WHY that particular pattern is used there.
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 척하다: 괜찮은 척하면서 — she is deliberately performing composure she does not feel (adjective 괜찮다 → -(으)ㄴ 척). 뻔하다: 울 뻔했다 — she genuinely nearly cried (울다 ㄹ-stem → 울 뻔했다); 잃어버릴 뻔했다 — she genuinely almost lost her wallet (잃어버리다 vowel stem → -ㄹ 뻔했다); 큰일 날 뻔했는데 — almost a disaster (나다 vowel stem → -ㄹ 뻔했는데). -나/-(으)ㄴ가 보다: 불만이 있으신가 봐서 — 불만이 있다 + honorific 있으시다 + -ㄴ가 봐; evidence-based inference from a blank expression. 스트레스를 많이 받으시나 봐 — 받다 is an action verb → -나 봐; the coworker is inferring from workplace clues.

culturalNote.title: 척하다 and the Art of Saving Face in Korean Workplaces
culturalNote.body: Korean workplace culture places enormous value on 눈치 (the ability to read the room) and not burdening others with every private feeling. 괜찮은 척하다 (pretending to be fine) can be a way to stay professional in public, especially during a presentation or meeting. If a coworker asks how you're doing on a busy Monday and you are exhausted, the socially expected first answer may still be 괜찮아요, with details saved for a closer conversation. Similarly, 모르는 척하다 (pretending not to know) can sometimes be a face-saving move: you notice something, but you leave room for the other person to handle it. 척하다 is not always noble or dishonest; the meaning depends on the relationship, the motive, and the situation.

inlineExercises.prompt: 배가 안 고___ 척했어요. 사실 엄청 배고팠어요. (Adjective: 고프다 = to be hungry)
inlineExercises.explanation: 고프다 is an adjective, so it takes the adjective modifier -(으)ㄴ: 고픈 척했어요. If you chose -프는 척, that's the action-verb pattern (-는 척) applied to an adjective, which is the #1 척하다 mistake. Always check: adjective → -(으)ㄴ 척, verb → -는 척.

inlineExercises.prompt: 하마터면 지하철을 ___ 뻔했어요. (놓치다 = to miss a train)
inlineExercises.explanation: -(으)ㄹ 뻔하다 uses the future/potential modifier -(으)ㄹ, not the present continuous -는. 놓치다 has a vowel-ending stem 놓치-, so it becomes 놓칠 뻔했어요. 놓치는 뻔했어요 is ungrammatical.

inlineExercises.prompt: 답장이 없는 걸 보니까 바쁘___ 봐요. (바쁘다 = to be busy — adjective)
inlineExercises.explanation: 바쁘다 is an adjective → use -(으)ㄴ가 보다. If it were an action verb (e.g., 일하다), you'd use -나 봐요. 바쁜가 봐요 = I guess they're busy (based on the no-reply evidence). 바쁘나 봐요 is colloquially used and understood, but 바쁜가 봐요 is the textbook-correct form.

inlineExercises.prompt: 다음 문장에서 틀린 것을 찾아보세요: '발표할 뻔해요.'
inlineExercises.explanation: Near-misses are finished events, so 뻔하다 must be in the past: 뻔했어요. 뻔해요 in the present would mean the near-miss is ongoing right now, which contradicts the logic of 뻔하다 — once you've ALMOST done something and DIDN'T, the moment is over.

inlineExercises.hint: 듣다 is an action verb. But you are pretending you ALREADY didn't hear — this is a past action, so use the past action modifier -(으)ㄴ: 들은 척. Add 못 before it for 'pretended not to have heard.'
inlineExercises.explanation: 못 들은 척했어요 means you acted as if you did not hear. Use the past modifier 들은 before 척 because the pretended state is 'not having heard.'

inlineExercises.prompt: You notice your friend has been very quiet lately and you want to say 'I'm guessing something happened.' Which is correct?
inlineExercises.explanation: 있다 is a stative verb (to exist/have) → use -나 봐요 for evidence-based inference. Option 1 (척해요) means PRETENDING something happened — totally different, implying your friend is faking. Option 3 (뻔했어요) means something ALMOST happened but didn't — also wrong; you're guessing it DID happen.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence correctly says 'She pretended to be sick'?
inlineExercises.explanation: 아프다 is an adjective. Adjectives take -(으)ㄴ in modifier position: 아프 + 은 → 아픈. Option 1 (아프는 척) wrongly uses the action-verb pattern -는. Option 3 (아팠는 척) incorrectly attaches -는 to a past tense stem — neither 아팠는 nor 척하다 work that way. The correct and only natural form is 아픈 척했어요.

inlineExercises.prompt: 친구___ 아픈가 봐요. (I guess my friend is sick.)
inlineExercises.explanation: 아프다 describes the friend, so 친구 takes the subject marker 가. 를 would make the friend an object, which does not fit an adjective sentence.
-(으)ㄹ 뻔했어요 means something almost happened but did not. 놓치다 becomes 놓칠 뻔했어요.
Adjectives take -(으)ㄴ before 척하다, so 바쁘다 becomes 바쁜 척했어요. This means you acted as if you were busy.

bullets: MASK (-는/-(으)ㄴ 척하다): put on a fake face — verb actions take -는 척, adjectives take -(으)ㄴ 척, past actions take -(으)ㄴ 척; 척하다 = deliberate pretense, not an honest impression
NEAR-MISS ALARM (-(으)ㄹ 뻔했어요): something almost happened but didn't — always past tense, add 하마터면 for drama, only with action verbs
EVIDENCE GUESS (-나 봐요 / -(으)ㄴ가 봐요): action verbs → -나 봐요, adjectives/이다 → -(으)ㄴ가 봐요; used for inferring about OTHER people from visible clues, not your own obvious feelings

writingTask.prompt: Write about a moment when you hid how you really felt, almost made a mistake, and guessed how someone else was feeling.
writingTask.hint: Use -는 척했어요 to pretend, -(으)ㄹ 뻔했어요 for the near miss, and -나 보다/-(으)ㄴ가 보다 to guess from evidence.
writingTask.model: 저는 안 무서운 척했어요. 그런데 너무 놀라서 소리를 지를 뻔했어요. 친구도 많이 무서웠나 봐요.
writingTask.modelEn: I pretended I wasn't scared. But I was so startled I almost screamed. My friend seems to have been very scared too.

canDo: Say someone is faking or putting on an act (-는 척하다)
Describe a close call that almost happened (-(으)ㄹ 뻔했다)
Guess about a situation from what I see or hear (-나 보다 / -(으)ㄴ가 보다)
Describe feelings and personality with 감동 · 두려움 · 성실하다 · 신중하다
